Rishi / Laura — reviewed. Key points and proposed language below. We should avoid an unlimited carve-out for SaaS unless it’s expressly tied to Redwood-managed physical equipment or willful misconduct/gross negligence by Redwood personnel. Suggested path:

1) Carve-out narrowness: Accept a carve-out for bodily injury and tangible property damage only where the injury/damage is directly caused by Redwood’s physical acts or Redwood-managed hardware that is installed on customer premises (e.g., a Redwood-provided edge appliance). Pure SaaS delivery or cloud-hosted inference can’t reasonably cause bodily harm or property damage; we should exclude those.

2) Cap / insurance: Rather than unlimited liability, require Customer to maintain commercial general liability (CGL) insurance with limits of at least $5M per occurrence and name Redwood as an additional insured for claims related to physical injury/property damage. Also propose a per-occurrence cap equal to the greater of $5M or 3x annual fees for the affected order, subject to evidence of insurance.

3) Indemnity carve-out alignment: If they want an indemnity, limit it to third-party claims directly resulting from Redwood’s physical acts or our on-site agents, and exclude indirect/consequential damages as already in the MSA.

Proposed redline snippet (high level):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitation of liability shall not apply to liability arising from (a) bodily injury (including death) or (b) damage to tangible property, to the extent such bodily injury or tangible property damage is caused by (i) Redwood’s willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (ii) Redwood-managed physical equipment installed at Customer premises. Customer shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of no less than $5,000,000 per occurrence and provide Redwood with certificates of insurance naming Redwood as an additional insured. In no event shall Redwood’s liability for such claims exceed the greater of $5,000,000 or three times the fees paid by Customer under the affected Order Form in the prior 12 months."

Practical note: If GreenGrid insists on an unlimited carve-out, this would escalate to exec/legal approval and would likely require repricing and insurance confirmation.

If you want, I can attach a redline PDF to send to the customer.

-Marissa
